findings.detail: The new text at encryption.md lines 110-118 documents a DEBUG-build path (`DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE`, `SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift`) that derives the SSD cache KEK from an on-disk file. It also documents an explicitly allowed ephemeral-key mode for ad hoc signed builds. The file-derived key is protected only by ownership, mode 0600 and volume encryption, not by the Secure Enclave. T-041 and its mitigations still treat every key as SE-rooted: K_lookup is derived from the SE-rooted KEK, a KEK wipe is the cryptographic purge, and lookup names are unfindable without the KEK. A key file that is readable, copied or backed up lets a disk observer or operator recompute the HMAC lookup tags and decrypt DBK3 files. That would reopen the leak #2 class that the HMAC design closed. The claim that release builds do not contain this path rests on code not supplied here, so the exclusion is unverified. Fix: update T-041 to record the debug and ephemeral KEK modes and the tag-recomputation and decryption exposure from the key file. Also state the build-time exclusion from release artifacts as a mitigation with a verification reference, such as a release-binary symbol check.
findings.title: Debug file-derived cache KEK is not in the threat model, which still says the KEK is SE-rooted
